form.en: yuefu ballad with lines of mixed length

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本。和古籍文本相比有几处不同：“拦道哭”古籍作“阑道哭”，“道旁”作“道傍”，“边庭”作“边亭”，“锄犁”的“犁”写法不同，“生女犹得嫁比邻”作“犹是”。前几处只是写法不同，意思一样；“犹得”是“还能够”，“犹是”是“还是”，意思也差不多。
text_note.en: This follows the commonly taught text. The old corpus differs in a few places. The words for "block the road", "roadside", "frontier" and "plow" are written with other forms of the characters, with the same meaning. In "a daughter can still marry a neighbor", the taught text says you dé (can still), while the corpus says you shì (is still). The meaning is nearly the same.

readings.en: Read yé. It is the same as the word for father.

readings.zh: “妻子”在这里是两个词：妻子和儿女，“子”读 zǐ。
readings.en: Here qī zǐ means wife and children, two words, so zǐ keeps its full tone.

readings.zh: 读 gān，冲上、直冲的意思。
readings.en: Read gān, meaning to rush up into.

readings.zh: “点行”的“行”，一般读 xíng，指征发人去服役；一说读 háng，指按名册点名、编入行伍。
readings.en: In diǎn xíng, this is usually read xíng: to send men off to serve. Another reading is háng, meaning ranks: men are called by name from a list and put into the ranks.

readings.zh: 读 hái，“还要、又要”的意思；也有人读 huán（回去）。
readings.en: Read hái, meaning "still, once again". Some read huán, meaning "go back".

readings.zh: “流血”在口语里常读 liú xiě，读书时一般读 xuè。
readings.en: In speech people often say xiě, but in reading aloud it is usually xuè.

readings.zh: 读 zhǎng，“长者”指年纪大、受尊敬的人。
readings.en: Read zhǎng. Zhǎng zhě means an older, respected person.

readings.zh: 读 mò，“埋没”是被埋掉、消失的意思。
readings.en: Read mò. Mái mò means buried and lost.

glosses.zh: 辚辚：车轮滚动的声音。
glosses.en: lín lín: the rumbling of cart wheels.

glosses.zh: 萧萧：马叫的声音。
glosses.en: xiāo xiāo: the neighing of horses.

glosses.zh: 行人：出征的人，就是被征去打仗的士兵。
glosses.en: xíng rén: the men going off to war, the conscripted soldiers.

glosses.zh: 耶娘：爹和娘。
glosses.en: yé niáng: father and mother.

glosses.zh: 妻子：妻子和儿女。
glosses.en: qī zǐ: wives and children.

glosses.zh: 走：跑。古时候“走”是跑的意思。
glosses.en: zǒu: to run. In old Chinese zǒu meant run, not walk.

glosses.zh: 尘埃：尘土。人马太多，扬起的尘土遮住了一切。
glosses.en: chén āi: dust. So many people and horses kick up dust that it hides everything.

glosses.zh: 咸阳桥：长安城西北渭水上的大桥，是往西北去的必经之路。
glosses.en: xián yáng qiáo: the great bridge over the Wei River northwest of Chang'an, on the road to the northwest.

glosses.zh: 顿足：跺脚。
glosses.en: dùn zú: to stamp one's feet.

glosses.zh: 拦道：拦在路上。
glosses.en: lán dào: blocking the road.

glosses.zh: 干云霄：直冲到天上。干，冲；云霄，高空。
glosses.en: gān yún xiāo: rising up into the sky. Gān means to rush into; yún xiāo means the high sky.

glosses.zh: 过者：路过的人。这里一般认为指诗人自己。
glosses.en: guò zhě: a passer-by. It is usually taken to be the poet himself.

glosses.zh: 但云：只说。
glosses.en: dàn yún: only says.

glosses.zh: 点行频：按名册征人去当兵，次数非常多。频，频繁。
glosses.en: diǎn xíng pín: men are called up from the lists again and again. Pín means often.

glosses.zh: 防河：守卫黄河一带。唐朝时常派兵到黄河以北防备外族入侵。
glosses.en: fáng hé: to guard the Yellow River region against raids from the north.

glosses.zh: 营田：军队在边疆一边驻守，一边种地。
glosses.en: yíng tián: to farm at the frontier while serving as a soldier.

glosses.zh: 里正：村里管事的小官，相当于村长。
glosses.en: lǐ zhèng: the village head.

glosses.zh: 与裹头：替他包头巾。古代男子成年要裹头巾，说明他去的时候年纪还小。
glosses.en: yǔ guǒ tóu: tied his head cloth for him. Grown men wore a head cloth, so this shows he was still very young.

glosses.zh: 戍边：守卫边疆。
glosses.en: shù biān: to guard the frontier.

glosses.zh: 边庭：边疆。
glosses.en: biān tíng: the frontier.

glosses.zh: 武皇：汉武帝。唐朝诗人常用汉朝的事说唐朝，这里实际是说唐玄宗。
glosses.en: wǔ huáng: Emperor Wu of Han. Tang poets often spoke of Han to mean their own time; here it really means Emperor Xuanzong of Tang.

glosses.zh: 开边：向外扩张领土。
glosses.en: kāi biān: to push the borders outward by war.

glosses.zh: 意未已：心思还没停止。
glosses.en: yì wèi yǐ: his wish has not stopped.

glosses.zh: 君不闻：你没有听说吗？古诗里常用来引起读者注意。
glosses.en: jūn bù wén: "Have you not heard?" A phrase old poems use to catch the reader's attention.

glosses.zh: 汉家：汉朝，这里借指唐朝。
glosses.en: hàn jiā: the Han dynasty, standing for the Tang.

glosses.zh: 山东：华山以东的地方，就是中原和东部广大地区。
glosses.en: shān dōng: the lands east of Mount Hua, the wide plains of the east.

glosses.zh: 千村万落：成千上万的村庄。
glosses.en: qiān cūn wàn luò: thousands of villages.

glosses.zh: 荆杞：荆棘和枸杞，都是野生的带刺灌木。田地没人种，就长满了野草荆棘。
glosses.en: jīng qǐ: thorny wild shrubs. With no one to farm, the fields are overgrown.

glosses.zh: 纵有：即使有。
glosses.en: zòng yǒu: even if there are.

glosses.zh: 健妇：身体强壮的妇女。
glosses.en: jiàn fù: strong women.

glosses.zh: 把锄犁：拿着锄头扶着犁耕地。
glosses.en: bǎ chú lí: holding the hoe and the plow.

glosses.zh: 陇亩：田地。陇，同“垄”，田里的土埂。
glosses.en: lǒng mǔ: the fields. Lǒng means the ridges of earth in a field.

glosses.zh: 无东西：分不清东西，形容庄稼长得乱七八糟，不成行列。
glosses.en: wú dōng xī: no east or west: the crops grow in a mess, with no proper rows.

glosses.zh: 况复：更何况。
glosses.en: kuàng fù: what is more.

glosses.zh: 秦兵：关中一带的士兵。关中古代是秦国的地方。
glosses.en: qín bīng: soldiers from the Guanzhong area, the old land of Qin.

glosses.zh: 耐苦战：能吃苦，能打硬仗。
glosses.en: nài kǔ zhàn: able to bear hard fighting.

glosses.zh: 被驱：被赶着走。
glosses.en: bèi qū: driven along.

glosses.zh: 不异：和……没有两样。
glosses.en: bù yì: no different from.

glosses.zh: 长者：年纪大、受尊敬的人。这里是士兵对诗人的尊称。
glosses.en: zhǎng zhě: an older, respected person. Here the soldier means the poet.

glosses.zh: 役夫：服役的人，士兵自称。
glosses.en: yì fū: a man serving his duty; the soldier means himself.

glosses.zh: 敢申恨：哪里敢说出心中的怨恨呢？申，说出。
glosses.en: gǎn shēn hèn: how would I dare to speak my grievance? Shēn means to state.

glosses.zh: 且如：就拿……来说。
glosses.en: qiě rú: take for example.

glosses.zh: 未休：没有让他们休息、回家。
glosses.en: wèi xiū: were not allowed to rest and go home.

glosses.zh: 关西卒：函谷关以西的士兵，也就是上面说的秦兵。
glosses.en: guān xī zú: soldiers from west of the Hangu Pass, the same men from Qin.

glosses.zh: 县官：这里指官府，朝廷。
glosses.en: xiàn guān: here it means the government.

glosses.zh: 索租：催要租税。
glosses.en: suǒ zū: to demand taxes.

glosses.zh: 信知：确实知道，真的明白了。
glosses.en: xìn zhī: truly know.

glosses.zh: 比邻：邻居，近处的人家。
glosses.en: bǐ lín: a neighbor.

glosses.zh: 随百草：跟野草一起烂掉，指战死在野外。
glosses.en: suí bǎi cǎo: rotting with the wild grass: dying out in the open.

glosses.zh: 青海头：青海湖边。唐朝军队和吐蕃常在这里打仗。
glosses.en: qīng hǎi tóu: the shores of Qinghai Lake, where Tang armies often fought the Tibetan kingdom.

glosses.zh: 烦冤：心里又烦又冤，满是委屈。
glosses.en: fán yuān: full of grief and wrong.

glosses.zh: 啾啾：凄惨的叫声，这里指鬼哭的声音。
glosses.en: jiū jiū: a thin, sad wailing; here, the crying of ghosts.

translation.zh: 战车隆隆地响，
translation.en: War carts rumble,

translation.zh: 战马萧萧地叫，
translation.en: war horses neigh,

translation.zh: 出征的人腰里都挂着弓和箭。
translation.en: and every man marching off has bow and arrows at his waist.

translation.zh: 爹娘、妻子和儿女跑着来送行，
translation.en: Fathers, mothers, wives and children run alongside to see them off,

translation.zh: 尘土飞扬，连咸阳桥都看不见了。
translation.en: and the dust is so thick that the Xianyang Bridge disappears.

translation.zh: 他们拉着衣服，跺着脚，拦在路上痛哭，
translation.en: They tug at clothes, stamp their feet, block the road and wail,

translation.zh: 哭声一直冲上云霄。
translation.en: and their crying rises straight into the clouds.

translation.zh: 路边经过的人问出征的人怎么回事，
translation.en: A passer-by on the roadside asks one of the marching men,

translation.zh: 出征的人只说：按名册征兵太频繁了。
translation.en: and the man only says: they call us up again and again.

translation.zh: 有的人十五岁就到北方去守黄河，
translation.en: Some went north at fifteen to guard the Yellow River,

translation.zh: 到了四十岁又被派到西边去种地守边。
translation.en: and at forty were sent west to farm the frontier.

translation.zh: 走的时候年纪太小，村长替他包上头巾，
translation.en: When they left, the village head tied their head cloths for them,

translation.zh: 回来时头发都白了，还要再去守边疆。
translation.en: and they came back white-haired, only to be sent to the border again.

translation.zh: 边疆上流的血已经多得像海水一样，
translation.en: At the frontier, blood has flowed like the sea,

translation.zh: 皇上扩张领土的心思还是没有停止。
translation.en: yet the emperor still wants to push the borders further.

translation.zh: 你没听说吗？华山以东的二百个州，
translation.en: Have you not heard? In the two hundred districts east of the mountains,

translation.zh: 成千上万的村庄都长满了荆棘野草。
translation.en: thousands of villages are overgrown with thorns.

translation.zh: 即使有强壮的妇女拿锄头扶犁耕地，
translation.en: Even where strong women take up hoe and plow,

translation.zh: 田里的庄稼也长得乱七八糟，不成行列。
translation.en: the crops in the fields grow in a mess, with no rows.

translation.zh: 更何况关中的士兵能吃苦、能打硬仗，
translation.en: Worse still, the men of Qin can bear hard fighting,

translation.zh: 所以被赶来赶去，跟狗和鸡没有两样。
translation.en: so they are driven here and there like dogs and chickens.

translation.zh: 您老人家虽然问起，
translation.en: Though you, sir, kindly ask,

translation.zh: 我们当兵的哪里敢说出心里的怨恨？
translation.en: how would a soldier like me dare speak his grievance?

translation.zh: 就拿今年冬天来说，
translation.en: Take this winter, for example:

translation.zh: 关西的士兵还没被放回家休息。
translation.en: the soldiers from west of the pass have not been sent home.

translation.zh: 官府却急着催要租税，
translation.en: Yet the officials press hard for taxes,

translation.zh: 租税从哪里来呢？
translation.en: and where are the taxes to come from?

translation.zh: 现在真的明白了，生男孩是坏事，
translation.en: Now we truly know that having a son is bad luck,

translation.zh: 反倒是生女孩好。
translation.en: and having a daughter is better.

translation.zh: 生了女孩，还能嫁给邻居，
translation.en: A daughter can still marry a neighbor nearby,

translation.zh: 生了男孩，只能战死在野外，和野草一起烂掉。
translation.en: but a son ends up buried among the wild grass.

translation.zh: 你没看见吗？在那青海湖边，
translation.en: Have you not seen, by the shores of Qinghai Lake,

translation.zh: 自古以来的白骨都没有人收埋。
translation.en: the white bones lying since long ago, with no one to bury them?

translation.zh: 新死的鬼满腹冤屈，旧死的鬼在痛哭，
translation.en: New ghosts grieve their wrongs and old ghosts weep,

translation.zh: 天阴下雨的时候，到处是凄惨的哭声。
translation.en: and when the sky is dark and wet with rain, their wailing fills the air.

background.zh: 这首诗大约写于唐玄宗天宝年间，一般认为在天宝十载（751年）前后。那时唐朝在边疆不断打仗，很多士兵死在战场上。据《资治通鉴》记载，天宝十载唐军攻打南诏（在今云南一带）大败，宰相杨国忠派人到处抓人当兵，家人哭着送行，哭声震动田野。一说这首诗写的是这件事；也有人认为写的是唐朝和吐蕃在西北的战争。杜甫看到这些，用一位士兵的话写下了这首诗。
background.en: This poem was written during the Tianbao years of Emperor Xuanzong, usually dated to around 751. The Tang empire was fighting wars at its borders all the time, and many soldiers died. A history book records that in 751 the Tang army was badly beaten while attacking Nanzhao, in today's Yunnan. The chief minister Yang Guozhong then sent men everywhere to seize people for the army. Their families followed them crying, and the sound filled the fields. One view is that the poem is about this. Others think it is about the wars with the Tibetan kingdom in the northwest. Du Fu saw such scenes and wrote this poem in a soldier's own words.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被称为“诗圣”。他的诗常常写普通百姓的苦难和国家的大事，所以被称为“诗史”，意思是用诗写成的历史。《兵车行》是他较早写百姓苦难的名篇，后来他又写了“三吏”“三别”等诗。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, often called the Sage of Poetry. His poems often tell of the suffering of ordinary people and the big events of the country. That is why they are called "history in poems". This is one of his early famous poems about people's suffering. Later he wrote more like it, such as the "Three Officials" and "Three Partings".

appreciation.zh: 诗一开头就像电影的大场面：车轮隆隆，战马嘶叫，尘土把大桥都遮住了，家人拉着衣服哭，哭声冲上天空。接着镜头拉近，一个过路人问，一个士兵回答。士兵说的话很平静，却句句扎心：十五岁去守河，四十岁还在守边；走时是孩子，回来头发白了还要再走。村子荒了，田地乱了，官府还来要税。最让人难过的是“生男恶，生女好”，这和平常人们重男轻女的想法正好相反，说明战争已经让人绝望了。最后写青海边的白骨和鬼哭，天阴下雨，声音凄凉。全诗从热闹的哭声开始，到冷冷的鬼哭结束，让人久久不能平静。
appreciation.en: The poem opens like a big scene in a film. Wheels rumble, horses neigh, dust hides the bridge, families cling to clothes and cry, and the crying rises into the sky. Then the camera moves in close. A passer-by asks, and a soldier answers. The soldier speaks calmly, but every word hurts. At fifteen he guarded the river; at forty he is still at the border. He left as a boy and came home white-haired, only to be sent out again. Villages lie empty, fields are a mess, and still the officials want taxes. Saddest of all, he says having a son is bad and a daughter is better. This is the opposite of what people usually believed then, which shows how hopeless the war has made them. At the end come the white bones by Qinghai Lake and the crying of ghosts in the dark rain. The poem starts with loud human weeping and ends with cold ghostly wailing. It stays with you for a long time.
